matches.quote: Ideally they should add a second device for at least one configuration, especially the (1+4) C = 4 state and the (2+4) transition.
The (1+N) devices sit at different twist angles (1.29°, 1.16°, 1.39°), so angle dependence and device-to-device spread cannot be judged.
The C = 3 to C = 4 transition in (2+4) L device D4 is not shown to be a gap-closing band-topology transition rather than a first-order switch
The C = 2 state at ν = 3/2 and the "incipient fractional Chern insulator" at ν = 7/3 are not established.
Novelty relative to Refs. [39–41, 54, 55] is not stated... Ref. [54] reports the same (2+4) L system, and Ref. [55] the twisted (1+N) family.
The authors should tabulate ρxy/(h/Ce²) and ρxx (in ohms), with uncertainties, at B = 0 and base temperature, for every claimed state
show whether the remanent B = 0 sign of ρxy is set by D or only by history... map the coercive field against ν and D
extract activation gaps of both states against D from the Extended Data Fig. 5 data and show whether the gap goes to zero at the boundary
Otherwise they should describe the effect as electric-field-controlled magnetization (chirality) reversal and present the Berry-curvature mechanism as a hypothesis.
Saying "opposite Chern numbers can coexist within the same scan direction" does not distinguish this from Ref. [32], because any hysteretic switch shows both signs
The authors should clarify the convention... fit dν/dB along the ρxx minimum or ρxy plateau and report C with an error bar
Ref. [39] is from the same group and covers twisted rhombohedral graphene with high Chern numbers, and D3 comes from it.

notes: C9 is marked 'partly' because P6/P13 ask to quantify Hall quantization accuracy and residual longitudinal resistance across states and temperatures in resistivity (rho_xy, rho_xx) rather than by tensor inversion to conductivity (sigma_xy, sigma_xx). C14 is marked 'partly' because P4 and P22 ask for history dependence, coercive field maps across (nu, D), and device-to-device reproducibility, but not repeated-trial switching success rates. C4 is marked 'partly' because P4 challenges the claimed distinction of the Fig. 3 switching from Ref. [32] and notes B-switching is generic while focusing on the switching mechanism.
